STATUS: fail

SUMMARY: One reproduced correctness problem: with the flag on, a slotted light-DOM target gets its slot in the shadow root hidden, so AT drops the target. The other criteria and hostile inputs I probed held, including a 1500-case seeded property run and a flag-off differential against HEAD. Two minor items: the flag-on path is about 14x slower than HEAD, and the flag-off test doesn't show that `<body>` is hidden.

FILES TOUCHED: none (probe files created and deleted; `git status` matches the starting state)

FINDINGS:
- [blocking] Slotted target: host H (body) has shadow `<slot>` plus `target` as a light child of H; `ariaHideOutside([target])` sets `aria-hidden="true"` on the slot. The target has no own attribute, but its flat-tree ancestor is hidden. Repro: `expect(slot).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden')` → Received `aria-hidden="true"`. Slots aren't in the criteria, so this is your call, but the target is effectively hidden from AT.
- [minor] Perf (not in criteria): 5000 shadow siblings + 200 announcers, flag on, one call takes 4731 ms; HEAD on the same light-DOM size takes 337 ms. The per-node loop over `visibleNodes` with `nodeContains` drives it.
- [minor] Flag-off test is weaker than it looks: with the flag off, both HEAD and the new code set `aria-hidden` on `<body>` when the target sits in a shadow root. The existing `expect(target).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden')` passes only because the target itself isn't marked. Pre-existing; not a regression.
- [minor] The `shadowDOM` describe calls `enableShadowDOM()` in `beforeAll` and never resets it; the flag-off test is correct only because it runs earlier in the file. Not reproduced as a failure.
- Not a bug: my first probe expected a non-target host containing a live announcer to be hidden. The host is correctly skipped, so its ancestors aren't hidden.

CHECKS:
- Probe: nested two levels, sibling host not on path (only host hidden, inner elements clear, restored) → pass
- Probe: target is a shadow host (siblings hidden, host and content visible) → pass
- Probe: append to hidden sibling host's shadow root, light container sibling, appended into hidden container → pass
- Probe: live announcer in a non-target sibling host, present before call and added later → pass
- Probe: element reparented from target into sibling position → hidden, pass
- Probe: two calls with targets in different shadow roots, revert out of order, then append → pass
- Probe: role=row in shadow root, cells hidden → pass
- Probe: custom root inside shadow root; custom root light element not containing host (no throw) → pass
- Probe: revert after host removed from document → pass
- Probe: keepVisible in shadow root → pass
- Probe: target nested in a shadow root within a target-containing host, revert restores siblings → pass
- Probe: nested calls, second call keeps host visible; first's shadow root observer disconnected while nested, re-observed after revert → pass
- Probe: `shouldUseInert` with shadow siblings, appended later, restore → pass
- Invariants (seeded property, 1500 random nested shadow trees): hide-everything-else, append rules, full restore → pass
- Differential flag-off vs HEAD (800 seeded light-DOM trees, sync and after mutations, snapshot of aria-hidden/role) → pass
- Flag-off: shadow sibling not hidden, late append not hidden → pass (but see body finding)
- Slot / slotted target → FAIL (blocking above)
- `yarn jest <probe>` and `yarn jest packages/@react-aria/overlays` as the handoff asks: I ran the probes only; the full-suite run is the orchestrator's.
- Dependency check: `@react-stately/flags` is 3.1.2 and matches the `yarn.lock` entry. I did not run `yarn install --immutable` (constraint: no `yarn install`).

OPEN QUESTIONS: Should slotted content be treated as "on the path" (don't hide slots that contain a target)? The criteria say nothing about slots. Is the flag-off `<body>` hiding in scope to fix?
